card.name: Ritual Dance of the Royal Drum
card.tagline: Sacred drumming-and-dance that once crowned Burundi's kings
card.profile: The ritual dance of the royal drum is a Burundian spectacle combining powerful synchronized drumming with dancing, heroic poetry and song (UNESCO; Wikipedia). At least a dozen drums, always an odd number, are arranged in a semicircle around a central Inkiranya drum; surrounding Amashako drums keep a continuous beat and Ibishikiso drums follow, while two or three drummers dance to the rhythm. Drummers enter and exit balancing the heavy drums on their heads. In ancient Burundi drums were sacred objects reserved for rituals such as coronations and royal funerals.
card.insight: The ingoma tradition dates to the 17th century and honored the monarchy — a king was said to have "ascended the drum." It was inscribed on UNESCO's Representative List of the Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity in 2014 (9.COM); a 2017 Presidential decree subsequently restricted performance to male players only.
related: Royal drum traditions of the Great Lakes
